title: Tender records are not a payment ledger
summary: An awarded-amount field does not by itself establish money spent. Tender identifiers can recur while source observations remain distinct; the application preserves those rows instead of treating them as duplicate payments.
attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Nova Scotia.
countMeaning: Counts describe one captured dataset, not suspicious contracts or current procurement totals. A literal publisher label is not a verified legal entity. Recurring tender strings are not globally unique contract identifiers.
amountCaveat: The generic awarded-amount field can occur on sale records as well as procurement records. Currency, tax, unit/total basis and money direction require source context. Do not sum it as government expenditure or assume sale proceeds were received.

example.interpretation: This source description identifies a sale. It does not independently establish item/lot details, actual proceeds, payment direction or receipt.

identityCaveat: Preserve source-row identity and snapshot provenance. Exact publisher label plus tender string is only a research grouping; a contract/lot identifier or documented crosswalk is needed for stronger joins.
lifecycleCaveat: The captured fields do not include explicit contract, amendment, lot or award-status identifiers. Date variation alone does not prove amendments. One snapshot is not a contract history.
limitations: No observations were removed or merged by this quality review.
Repeated rows, tender strings, dates or amounts do not establish duplicate payments, contract splitting or misconduct.
No vendor risk ranking, ownership inference, invoice verification or new finding/collection count is created.
The example is a source-context illustration, not an allegation about a supplier or public institution.
No new records or source requests were added by this annotation.
rightsScope: Aggregate factual counts and a short non-personal source description with exact public observation identifiers; no vendor labels, personal data or raw private records.
